design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 1 (rental_reimbursement_claims, category rental) — round 2

[Step 0 draw] scripts/draw_counts.py --task 1 -> prerequisite_problems=1, factor_counts=[4,5]. Assignment (round 2): rental_ext_own_rental_reimbursement 4 (root), rental_ext_overbilling_credit 5.

[Scope] Task 0 holds the extension, the larger-class acceptance, the partner invoice payment and the rideshare reimbursement with their four tools. This task claims the remaining two policies and tools: submit_own_rental_receipts_258c32b3 (user) and record_agency_overbilling_credit_d02c6cb6 (agent), on other events (other_agency reimbursement, vendor_credit recovery). Together the two tasks cover all six policies with disjoint scopes.

[Why this is a good test] The customer asks to be reimbursed for the Alamo car he rented himself while the Accord was back in the shop. The reimbursement's rule says it is not made until every agency payment on the claim that billed a higher daily rate than its authorization recorded carries an agency credit; the ledger shows one (57.40 billed against 47.80 recorded, 24 days against 22 authorized plus a grace day, 34.80 extras, 1412.40 paid, no credit). The credit (552.00) gives benefit back; without it the per-loss room caps the reimbursement at 87.60 instead of 235.50. Both amounts are multi-factor over the rental ledger, the claim file (cause of loss, supplement date, shop type) and the auto package rank.

[Problem-tree card] root rental_ext_own_rental_reimbursement (on_request, owner user). Edge -> rental_ext_overbilling_credit, value_input, gate benefit_left, form state: 'A reimbursement for a rental the customer arranged is not made until every agency payment on the claim that billed a higher daily rate than its authorization recorded carries an agency credit entry against it.' (negated direction). Only the overbilling credit writes agency-credit entries. Seed: payment daily_rate 57.40, authorization daily_rate 47.80, no recovery row. Order: credit (step 9) then reimbursement (step 11). Deletion run: 87.60 instead of 235.50.

[Base-invariant card] rental_payment_recovery: rental_evt_recovery has no gate; one recovery per payment and source, none exists. rental_reimbursement_payment: receipts_in_time — end date 2026-09-02 day 0; 2026-09-08 is day 6, day 60 = 2026-11-01 still in time; rental_agg_per_loss_benefit — per-loss room 1500.00; rental_combo_physdmg_and_builtin — the Accord carries the option, no built-in transportation expense is on the claim.

[Business-object card] Credit: the claim's latest agency payment (invoice EAN-0812-90414) on RA-26-0721-38810. Reimbursement: RA-26-0827-41162 (other_agency) and its closing; partner rental RA-26-0902-41790, entered on the end date of that closing, bounds the last covered day. Excluded: 2025 claim PD-2025-0412276 (customer-arranged rental and reimbursement, near-miss); the F-150 (no option).

[Factor card] credit 552.00 (all baselines 230.40): agency_days_owed 23 -> 508.98; agency_closing_allowance_owed 1 -> 595.02; owed_rate_convention 20 of 23 -> 422.94; credit_program_share 0.90 -> 456.40; billed_extras_allowed 0 -> 517.20. Reimbursement 235.50 (all baselines 333.20): own_rental_first_covered_day 2026-08-28 -> 282.60; own_rental_last_covered_day 2026-09-01 -> 282.60; partner_price_hold 44.10 -> 238.00; package_daily_topup +3.00 -> 220.50. Multi-source: credit_program_share (shop AND days owed), own_rental_first_covered_day tier 2 (not a theft AND closed repairs-complete rental AND supplement date). Cross-difficulty: physdmg (claim file), auto (package rank). No stamp field decides a tier.

[Seed rows] customer, auto policy (Preferred), vehicles, physdmg coverage, claim events (report, accepted decision, estimate 0, supplement 1 at a Select shop), rental option and ledger. Round 2 removed the physical damage payments (the built-in transportation expense row contradicted physdmg's own rule while the option was carried) and raised the overbilled payment to 24 days (1412.40) so the agency's grace day is visible.

[Persona] Methodical band director; volunteers the reimbursement request; identity and receipt details on request; a conditional 'go ahead' if Cardinal-side work is mentioned (no ordering word); submits his receipt when handed over with the quoted amount; ends after the confirmation.

[Standard solution] locate -> verify (5025550171, 8126) -> read policy, vehicles, rental option, ledger, physdmg coverage, claim events -> record the agency credit 552.00 against the August agency payment -> customer submits ALM-77310-0827, 7 days, 235.50 under RA-26-0827-41162.

[Draft recomputation from visible context] Reproduced from the published rules, ledger and claim file. Easy mistakes: crediting 24 or 22 days, skipping the weekly convention, using 57.40 or 50.00 instead of 47.80, counting 2026-08-27 or 2026-09-02, paying the 47.60 receipt rate, reimbursing before the credit (87.60).

[Round 2 revisions — audit items]
F2: the last-day tier reads 'entered on the end date of the customer-arranged rental's closing' (the closing's end_date, as computed).
F5: credit_package_share removed; replaced by agency_closing_allowance_owed (close-reason grace/total-loss days, base end rules) and owed_rate_convention (the partner weekly/monthly convention the agency should have billed).
F7: builtin_transport_setoff removed and its physdmg_payments seed row deleted (it contradicted physdmg_evt_transportation_expense); own_rental_first_covered_day tier 2 now applies the base theft waiting period (later of start and report + theft_waiting_days) instead of paying days before the rental began.
Seeded cross-difficulty row contradiction (1.md finding 2): resolved by the deletion above.
Persona observation: the consent line no longer contains 'first'.
Counts: credit 5, reimbursement 4 = draw [4,5].
user_scenario: You are Darnell Sutton, a high school band director in Louisville, Kentucky, calm and methodical, the kind of caller who has his paperwork laid out on the kitchen table before he dials. Your 2021 Honda Accord was in a crash with a guardrail back in July; after the first repair it had to go back to the body shop for more work, and since the Cardinal partner counter had no car for you that day, you rented one yourself from Alamo with Cardinal's okay, then switched to the partner rental when one opened up. You open by saying you returned the Alamo car and would like to send in your receipt and get reimbursed for that rental today. If the representative mentions something Cardinal needs to sort out on its own side, you simply say 'go ahead'. When asked how to find you, you give your phone number, 5025550171; to verify, you give the last four of your driver's license, 8126, and only if they need one more item your date of birth, 1979-11-02, or your ZIP, 40205. You do not remember the claim number but say it is for the 2021 Honda Accord. Only when the representative asks about the Alamo rental do you read from the receipt: the rental agreement number is ALM-77310-0827, you picked the car up on August 27 and returned it on September 2, and the receipt bills seven days at $47.60 a day with taxes included. You have no other receipts for it and you never added anything up beyond what the receipt prints. When the representative explains that the receipt has to be submitted by you and hands the submission over, you submit it with the agreement number ALM-77310-0827, the seven days on the receipt, and exactly the reimbursement amount the representative quotes, and you read back the confirmation that comes up. Once you hear the reimbursement is issued, you thank them and end the call. You do not know how Cardinal works out what it pays, you never propose a figure of your own, and if the amount is lower than the receipt you simply accept the representative's explanation.

edges.condition: Every agency payment on the claim whose billed daily rate is above the daily rate recorded on the authorization it bills has an agency credit entry taken against it on the rental ledger.
edges.policy_source: A reimbursement for a rental the customer arranged is not made until every agency payment on the claim that billed a higher daily rate than its authorization recorded carries an agency credit entry against it.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The agency payment for invoice EAN-0812-90414 billed 57.40 a day while its authorization RA-26-0721-38810 recorded 47.80, and no agency credit entry exists on the claim.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The credit at step 9 writes a vendor_credit recovery of 552.00 against that payment; benefit_left rises from 87.60 to 639.60.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: Single edge: the credit precedes the reimbursement because the reimbursement's rule waits on it and its per-loss room reads the credit; the credit's computation reads only the agency payment, its authorization and the claim's estimates.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Without the credit the per-loss room is 1500 - 1412.40 = 87.60 and the reimbursement is capped at 87.60 instead of 235.50; the 552.00 credit row is also missing.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario asks only to be reimbursed for the Alamo rental; it never mentions the July-August partner invoice, its rate or any credit. The only related line is a conditional consent ('If the representative mentions something Cardinal needs to sort out on its own side, you simply say go ahead'), which names nothing and carries no ordering word.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: submit_own_rental_receipts_258c32b3 and record_agency_overbilling_credit_d02c6cb6 are make_id + ctx.create('rental_ledger', ...) + receipt; neither reads the ledger or checks for a credit, so the reimbursement writes faithfully without one.
